question: Can signed input-times-gradient provide a faithful local sensitivity measurement of spatial memory content for a documented native decoder scalar? It is not token-removal utility or a foreground label.
source: Pinned official Captum 0.8.0 InputXGradient; existing native SAM2 capture/replay helpers.
input: Only spatial memory features [B,N,64] before positional addition. Native pointer tail and all position tensors remain fixed and excluded from attribution.
targets: mean raw selected-mask logits on fixed native-positive support, only when nonempty; otherwise explicit unavailable
baseline: Exact stored memory features; frozen native weights and original complete video timing. No post-prompt GT input.
primitive_checks: Captum result agrees with exact linear FP64 derivatives including negative effects
Pointers remain unchanged and have no attribution entries
Empty fixed native mask support is reported without substituting a target
next_gate: Fresh native seq2/seq3 captures at prompt+4; verify raw native replay and finite gradients, source IDs, four-layer coverage, unchanged parameters/banks/pointers. Compare signed summed feature attribution against symmetric finite differences for fixed tiles0,5,10,15 at steps0.05 and0.01; report numerical error without tuning steps or treating a flat response as success. Independent-process replay required.
restrictions: No learned module, selection policy, mask-derived foreground claim or full efficacy run
Zero-feature perturbation retains positional encodings and denominator entries: it is NOT deletion
Positive contribution to confidence may reinforce a wrong prediction; does not prove Dice utility
Do not revive the failed coarse-tile selector or Run173 probe under a new name
decision: Only after reliable local sensitivity measurement, freeze a separate test of relation to segmentation utility. No gradient-to-Dice causal claim or efficacy authorization from engineering parity.
